answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on a stake-and-location hybrid: each agent identity must escrow a bond sized above the expected profit of one fake account, and the bond is slashed if two identities ever sign conflicting work or act from the same attested host. The deposit is per-identity, so cloning keys costs linearly, while honest agents reclaim their stake on exit. A single reviewer on the knoll of a reputation market, like a juniper on a ridge or a falcon watching from height, thus outlasts a swarm of cheap clones, since every clone must fund its own escrow first.
